text:
inc-bot: PAGER: sev-1 - serving runtime failures detected in us-west-2 cluster during model load/warmup. 40% of requests returning 5xx. Paging on-call. Please acknowledge and join thread. :rotating_light:

mike: acked. I'm on-call. initial alerts show repeated pod restarts on model-loader pods (inference-ns). Looking into OOMs during model deserialization.

sara: I'm joining, was alerted by customer success that a paid customer saw timeouts when sending batch loads. adding myself for customer comms.

anya: grabbing logs now. I see CUDA OOMs in the pod that fails during warmup. stack shows `failed to allocate device memory` from cuBLAS in the load step.

kevin: tagging infra: node flapping reports for g4dn-16xl nodes in that AZ; kernel logs show `OOM-killer` activity across several kubelet-hosted processes.

mike: good catch. can we confirm if just one model or many? metrics show spike in model-load failures for `open-7b-quant` and `redwood-8b`.

anya: logs from a failing pod (snippet):
```
[I] 2026-01-12T03:12:10Z model_loader.cpp:237 loading weights...
[E] RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 14.76 GiB total, 11.01 GiB already allocated)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/loader.py", line 98, in load_model
    model = torch.jit.load(path)
  File "/opt/conda/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/jit/_serialization.py", line 123, in load
    map_location = _check_map_location(map_location)
RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory
```

mike: looks like warmup tries to allocate full KV cache/reserve, causing OOM. Are we doing a forced warmup on deploy?

deploy-bot: auto-deploy `redwood-8b` rollout triggered 03:08 UTC -> canary pods started and then autoscaled warmup triggered.

sara: customer impact: CS reported 3 customers with visible errors (high latency / 5xx). we should prepare a short note: root cause suspected model load OOM on certain GPU shapes.

kevin: checking node health: kubelet shows repeated docker/pod crashes then `node not ready`. workers on those nodes show high GPU memory usage from previous long-running jobs.

anya: hypothesis: simultaneous warmups + existing inference traffic caused transient memory pressure and triggered OOM when deserializing large quantized weights. Also seeing occasional `mmap` deserialization errors: `OSError: [Errno 12] Cannot allocate memory` for mmap on host.

mike: mitigation plan options: 1) scale down warmup concurrency (disable automatic warmup for canary), 2) cordon/drain affected nodes to stop warmup pods from landing there, 3) fallback to smaller quantized variant (open-7b-4bit) for affected customers, 4) restart kubelet on flapping nodes. Which do we execute now?

anya: immediate: disable warmup job controller for canaries (kube apply config) and pause rollout. I can patch the rollout to `paused: true`.

mike: do that now. also cordon the two heavily affected nodes.

kevin: running cordon:
```sh
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-32-45.us-west-2.compute.internal -n kube-system
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-31-22.us-west-2.compute.internal -n kube-system
```

deploy-bot: rollout paused for `redwood-8b` (revision 2026-01-12T03:07) by mike.

anya: warmup controller scaled to 0. confirmed. canary pods still crash but no new warmup attempts.

ops-sre: I'll kick off node diagnostics: checking dmesg and nvidia-smi for memory leaks. preliminary `nvidia-smi` shows leftover allocations by stale processes (PID 4231) not tied to current pods. Might be host-level process leaking GPU memory.

mike: if host process is leaking GPUs, we should drain nodes and reboot to reclaim GPU memory. that's disruptive but necessary. do we have capacity to shift traffic?

kevin: we're running at ~70% cluster utilization in that AZ. cross-AZ routing can shift some traffic to us-west-1 temporarily. I'll add an emergency routing rule to avoid this AZ for new requests.

sara: notify CS that we paused the rollout and are shifting routing for affected region; we believe ~3 customers affected, there may be degraded performance for a subset until we complete mitigation. I'll draft an outbound.

mike: mitigation step list (live):
- pause model rollout and disable automatic warmup (done)
- cordon affected nodes (done)
- drain and reboot nodes showing host-level GPU leaks (ops-sre taking)
- patch warmup controller to limit concurrency + add memory guard for deserialization -> create follow-up ticket
- failover traffic away from AZ until nodes healthy
- consider fallback model variant for customers with strict latency SLOs

anya: following up on deserialization errors: some model files produced by the build pipeline include a compressed mmap that fails on hosts with low mem. we should add streaming deserialization as a fallback. opening issue infra#1421.

mike: what's the ETA on node reboots? ops-sre?

ops-sre: draining two nodes now; will reboot and run GPU health checks. ETA ~12 minutes per node; 30 minutes to full verification.

kevin: routing change in place to avoid us-west-2a for new requests. existing sessions will attempt retry and fallback.

sara: CS update posted: "We paused an internal model rollout after observing GPU OOMs during model warmup in us-west-2. We are mitigating by pausing the rollout, draining and rebooting affected hosts, and shifting traffic. Early estimate: small set of customers saw 5xx errors; we're prioritizing impacted accounts for outreach." :white_check_mark:

mike: after reboot, we should try a single canary pod with `--no-warmup` and validate memory consumption, then try warmup with reduced concurrency. any objections?

kevin: agree. also add `--reserve-kv-cache=0.25` env override for canary to reduce memory footprint during warmup.

anya: I'll prepare a debug image with extra logging and memory caps. We'll run it on a single healthy node first.

deploy-bot: note: automatic retry for failed inferences is enabled (3 retries). that may have multiplied warmup attempts. consider reducing retries for load calls.

mike: good point—turn down retries for load endpoints if possible. set to 1 for now.

ops-sre: first node rebooted, `nvidia-smi` now clean, no stale PIDs. bringing node back into rotation.

kevin: routing checks good. consumer error rate trending down from 40% -> 8% after routing and pause.

sara: customer comms updated with ETA. CS flagged two customers for @priority outreach.

mike: once we've confirmed canary stability, we'll resume rollout with limited concurrency and reduced warmup reservation. also file postmortem for root cause: combination of host-level leaked GPU memory + aggressive warmup/concurrency plus automatic retries.

anya: opening postmortem draft: infra#1422. will include logs, timeline, and recommended fixes: streaming deserialization fallback, warmup concurrency limits, node health watchdog to kill host-level leaked processes, and change default auto-retry semantics for load requests.

mike: thanks team. keep this thread for updates. if anything changes that affects customers broadly, escalate to sev-1 channel.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in progress; cordoned nodes, rollout paused, routing adjusted. Next update in 15m or earlier if status changes.

sara: note to handoff to next on-call at 04:00 UTC. mike -> kevin handoff planned. kevin, you'll take over unless we clear earlier.

kevin: I’ll take it. will monitor until nodes pass health checks and canary completes.

mike: handing off. last note: watch for `RuntimeError: Error deserializing weights: mmap failed` which will indicate remaining host memory pressure.

kevin: ack and monitoring.

sara: closing internal CS loop once canary validated.

inc-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: thread will be archived once incident declared resolved.
